people.name: Kim Seok-jin
people.description: Kim Seok-jin is a South Korean singer and songwriter who performs with the boy band BTS. The group achieved a milestone by becoming the first Korean act to reach the top of the US Billboard chart with their 2018 studio album Love Yourself: Tear. Additionally, BTS earned the distinction of being the fastest group since The Beatles to secure four US No.1 albums, accomplishing this feat in under two years. They also marked the first time an Asian act charted a No.1 song in the US since Kyu Sakamoto achieved it with 'Sukiyaki' in 1963.

people.name: Jelly Roll
people.description: American rapper, singer, and songwriter Jelly Roll, also known as Jason Bradley DeFord, released his tenth studio album, Beautifully Broken, in 2024. The album became his first US No.1 album.

people.name: Adam Blackstone
people.description: Adam Blackstone is a multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, producer, and bassist. He has directed and performed in shows alongside Justin Timberlake, Jay-Z, Kanye West, Eminem, Janet Jackson, Dr. Dre, The Jonas Brothers, Al Green, The Isley Brothers, Angie Stone, Mike Posner, Steve Tirpak, Al Jarreau, and Maroon 5.

people.name: Kate Rusby
people.description: English folk singer-songwriter Kate Rusby released the indie album Awkward Annie in 2007, which reached No. 2. Earlier, in June 2006, her collaboration and duet with Ronan Keating titled 'All Over Again' reached No. 6 on the UK Singles Chart.

people.name: Justin Welch
people.description: English musician Justin Welch is best known for drumming in Elastica, Suede, and subsequently in Lush and The Jesus and Mary Chain. Additionally, Welch established the Britpop supergroup Me Me Me alongside Blur bassist Alex James and Stephen Duffy, the frontman of The Lilac Time.

people.name: Jay-Z
people.description: Shawn Carter, known professionally as Jay-Z, is an American rapper, record executive, and businessman. In 1994, he established Roc-A-Fella Records as a co-founder to put out his first two studio albums. Jay-Z entered into marriage with singer Beyoncé in 2008. Centered around a rags-to-riches story, his music reflects a net worth of $2.6 billion as of 2025. Jay-Z holds 14 No.1 albums, sharing a tie with Drake for the second-highest total achieved by a solo artist. On the Billboard Hot 100, he has reached the top position four times: as a lead artist with the 2009 track 'Empire State of Mind' featuring Alicia Keys, and as a featured guest on three songs—'Heartbreaker' in 1999 alongside Mariah Carey, 'Crazy in Love' in 2003 with Beyoncé, and 'Umbrella' in 2007 with Rihanna.

people.name: Dionne Farris
people.description: American singer and songwriter Dionne Farris gained prominence after appearing on the 1992 hit single 'Tennessee' by the hip hop group Arrested Development. She subsequently achieved wider fame with her 1994 debut album, Wild Seed - Wild Flower, which included the Top 40 single 'I Know'.

people.name: Adamski
people.description: Adamski, whose birth name is Adam Tinley, is an English DJ, musician, singer, and record producer. In 1990, he achieved a UK No.1 single with 'Killer', which was created in collaboration with Seal.

people.name: Danny Weinkauf
people.description: Danny Weinkauf is the bassist for the American alternative rock band They Might Be Giants. The group achieved a UK No.6 single in 1990 with 'Birdhouse In Your Soul'. Additionally, the band has earned two Grammy Awards, receiving one in 2002 for the track 'Boss of Me' and another in 2009 for 'Here Come the 123s'.

people.name: Gary Rossington
people.description: American musician Gary Rossington is best known as a founder of the southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd, which released the 1974 US No. 8 single 'Sweet Home Alabama', the 1977 US No. 5 album Street Survivors, and the 1982 UK No. 21 single 'Freebird'. Rossington passed away at his home in Milton, Georgia, on 5 March 2023 at the age of 71.

people.name: Southside Johnny
people.description: American singer-songwriter Southside Johnny fronted the band Southside Johnny and the Asbury Jukes. Long regarded as the Grandfather of the New Jersey Sound, Southside Johnny was acknowledged by Jon Bon Jovi as his reason for singing.

people.name: Terry Woods
people.description: Terry Woods is an Irish folk musician, songwriter, singer, and multi-instrumentalist. He was a member of the Irish-British Celtic punk band The Pogues, which scored the 1987 UK No.8 single 'The Irish Rover'.

people.name: Dennis Wilson
people.description: American singer, songwriter, and musician Dennis Wilson co-founded The Beach Boys. He is best known as the drummer for the group and as the middle brother of fellow band members Brian and Carl Wilson. The Beach Boys achieved a No. 1 single in both the UK and the US in 1966 with 'Good Vibrations', alongside more than 25 additional UK Top 40 singles. In his final years, Wilson dealt with substance abuse, which worsened existing tensions with certain bandmates. Pacific Ocean Blue (1977), his only solo album released during his lifetime, received warm reviews. Following a heavy day of drinking on 28th December 1983, he drowned while swimming from his boat, which was moored in Marina Del Rey, California. Dennis was the sole true surfer in the Beach Boys.

people.name: Hux Brown
people.description: Jamaican guitarist Hux Brown played on numerous successful reggae and rocksteady recordings throughout the 1960s and 1970s, and subsequently joined Toots and the Maytals as a member. At the age of 75, he passed away on 18 June 2020 in Oakland, California.

people.name: Chris Hillman
people.description: American musician Chris Hillman achieved a 1965 UK and US No. 1 single with 'Mr Tambourine Man' as a member of The Byrds. He additionally played in the Flying Burrito Brothers and The Souther, Hillman, Furay Band. Hillman played a key role in developing country rock.

people.name: Bob Mosley
people.description: Bob Mosley is a member of the American psychedelic rock band Moby Grape, which gained recognition for their 1967 debut album, Moby Grape. The group was distinguished as one of the few bands in which every member functioned as both a lead vocalist and a songwriter.

people.name: Freddy Cannon
people.description: American rock and roll singer Freddy Cannon secured a 1959 No.3 single in both the US and the UK with 'Way Down Yonder In New Orleans', alongside the US No.13 hit 'Tallahassee Lassie'. In 1962, Cannon acted alongside Bobby Vee, Johnny Tillotson, and others in the UK-produced film Just for Fun. Following a brief battle with cancer, Cannon passed away at the age of 89 while in hospice care in Oxnard, California, on July 17, 2026.

people.name: Tommy Morgan
people.description: Tommy Morgan is an American harmonicist and session musician. Regarded as one of the most frequently heard harmonica players globally, his career features collaborations with numerous prominent artists, such as Randy Newman, Carpenters, Carly Simon, Neil Diamond, Dolly Parton, Linda Ronstadt, and James Taylor.

works.title: Life to Go
works.eventDescription: American country music singer and musician Stonewall Jackson passed away in Nashville, Tennessee, at age 89. Late 1958 marked his entry into the country Top 40, achieved with the song 'Life to Go', which was written by a young George Jones.

works.title: Eagle Rock
works.eventDescription: Wayne Duncan, who played bass for the Australian rock band Daddy Cool, passed away after suffering a stroke. The group's first single, 'Eagle Rock', released in 1971, held the No.1 spot on the Australian singles chart for a period of ten weeks. Additionally, their debut LP, Daddy Who? Daddy Cool, came out in July 1971, climbed to No.1, and achieved the milestone of becoming the first Australian album to surpass 100,000 in sales.

works.title: Hot Rats
works.eventDescription: The multi-instrumentalist, producer, and composer Frank Zappa passed away from prostate cancer. He produced numerous albums both independently and alongside The Mothers Of Invention, which featured releases such as the 1969 record 'Hot Rats' and the 1974 record 'Apostrophe'. Zappa put out 'Freak Out' in 1966, marking one of the earliest double albums in rock music as well as an early concept album, though it came a week after Bob Dylan's Blonde on Blonde. In 1967, he wed Adelaide Gail Sloatman, and the couple had four children named Moon Unit, Dweezil, Ahmet Emuukha Rodan, and Diva Thin Muffin Pigeen.

works.eventDescription: 'Beat Surrender' gave The Jam their fourth UK No.1 and final single, topping the UK singles chart. The band broke up in 1983, after which frontman Paul Weller created the Style Council and subsequently pursued a solo career.

works.title: Anarchy in the UK
works.eventDescription: Staff members at the record label EMI initiated a strike, declining to handle the packaging of The Sex Pistols track 'Anarchy In The UK.'

works.title: Stairway to Heaven
works.eventDescription: Led Zeppelin began a two-week reign at No. 1 on the UK chart with their Four Symbols record, which is also called Led Zeppelin IV. The release includes the eight-minute song "Stairway To Heaven" and spent nearly five years on the US chart—falling short by just one week—while surpassing 23 million US sales.

works.title: Smoke on the Water
works.eventDescription: The Montreux Casino in Switzerland burnt to the ground during a gig by Frank Zappa. The incident is immortalized by Deep Purple's 'Smoke On The Water'. In 1967 the Casino became the venue for the Montreux Jazz Festival, which was the brainchild of music promoter Claude Nobs. On the night of the blaze, Nobs saved several young people who, thinking they would be sheltered from the flames, had hidden in the casino from the blaze. A recording of the outbreak and fire announcement can be found on a Frank Zappa Bootleg album titled Swiss Cheese / Fire.

works.eventDescription: Danny Weinkauf is the bassist for the American alternative rock band They Might Be Giants. The group achieved a UK No.6 single in 1990 with 'Birdhouse In Your Soul'. Additionally, the band has earned two Grammy Awards, receiving one in 2002 for the track 'Boss of Me' and another in 2009 for 'Here Come the 123s'.

works.title: Sweet Home Alabama
works.eventDescription: American musician Gary Rossington is best known as a founder of the southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd, which released the 1974 US No. 8 single 'Sweet Home Alabama', the 1977 US No. 5 album Street Survivors, and the 1982 UK No. 21 single 'Freebird'. Rossington passed away at his home in Milton, Georgia, on 5 March 2023 at the age of 71.

works.title: Good Vibrations
works.eventDescription: American singer, songwriter, and musician Dennis Wilson co-founded The Beach Boys. He is best known as the drummer for the group and as the middle brother of fellow band members Brian and Carl Wilson. The Beach Boys achieved a No. 1 single in both the UK and the US in 1966 with 'Good Vibrations', alongside more than 25 additional UK Top 40 singles. In his final years, Wilson dealt with substance abuse, which worsened existing tensions with certain bandmates. Pacific Ocean Blue (1977), his only solo album released during his lifetime, received warm reviews. Following a heavy day of drinking on 28th December 1983, he drowned while swimming from his boat, which was moored in Marina Del Rey, California. Dennis was the sole true surfer in the Beach Boys.

works.title: Way Down Yonder in New Orleans
works.eventDescription: American rock and roll singer Freddy Cannon secured a 1959 No.3 single in both the US and the UK with 'Way Down Yonder In New Orleans', alongside the US No.13 hit 'Tallahassee Lassie'. In 1962, Cannon acted alongside Bobby Vee, Johnny Tillotson, and others in the UK-produced film Just for Fun. Following a brief battle with cancer, Cannon passed away at the age of 89 while in hospice care in Oxnard, California, on July 17, 2026.
